notes:
copilot mid-turn follow-up, driven on the plain-Enter STEERING path. Copilot has TWO mid-turn input paths (app.js, CLI 1.0.77): the composer's onSubmit Zf sends with mode = ne?.queued ? "enqueue" : "immediate", and ne.queued is set ONLY by the key predicate hcn (ctrl+q / ctrl+return). So plain Enter mid-turn is STEERING (mode:"immediate") and Ctrl+Q is the true queue. Neither path writes anything at typing time: send() with mode:"immediate" stashes via addImmediateMessagesIfProcessing and returns before any emit.

OBSERVED SHAPE (live 2026-08-03, CLI 1.0.77 — replaces the assessment's provisional emission claim): the steered follow-up is NOT folded into turn 1. Copilot closes turn 1 and materialises the message inside a NEW turn, writing assistant.turn_end → assistant.turn_start → user.message within ~70 ms, then answering both requests in that second turn ("done" then "42") and closing it with a second assistant.turn_end. Reproduced identically across two consecutive recordings.

THE SCENARIO'S INVARIANTS STILL HOLD, and this is the load-bearing observation: the daemon emits NO ready flicker at that boundary. The three boundary lines land inside one activity-debounce pass whose NET state is "turn open", so the classifier sees working throughout — the whole run is exactly three transitions (presession ready, real session born working, one working→ready settle at the end) with zero flickers. NO queuedTurnSplitter seam is involved: the copilot parser does not implement SplitsQueuedFollowUpTurns, and tailer's updateMidPassTurnBoundary does not arm here. Because both turn_ends are real, wait_turn returns at the FIRST one — hence the long trailing sleep, without which the run is torn down before the final turn_end's debounce window closes.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED from the live recording: the transient proc-<PID> row is born ready and remains the presession anchor, but the REAL session is born DIRECTLY into working (reason "new session created") because copilot writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so the open turn is already on disk at discovery. Session birth and turn start are ONE phase; the pre-recording spec's separate ready birth does not exist.

OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from the transcript through the shared capacity price map; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)

The real session reconciles under a DIFFERENT session id (the session-state directory name) once the first prompt (a shell `sleep 10`, so the turn stays working long enough to type into) creates events.jsonl, and is born DIRECTLY into working because the file already carries the open turn
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)

A plain-text follow-up is typed into the TUI mid-turn and steered in. State must stay working through its arrival — no flicker to ready at the turn_end → turn_start → user.message boundary copilot writes for it (spec bullets 1 and 2), and no flicker to waiting (--allow-all means no permission.requested is ever written)
The cycle ends at ready (spec bullet 3) — the SECOND assistant.turn_end settles the turn that consumed the follow-up, and the session returns to ready once its activity-debounce window closes
